_comment: SD18. Rootstone, the first progression-tier material. `data/recipes/recipes.json`'s own `_comment_scope` said this would land in its own file rather than growing that one, and `ralph/DONE.md`'s R4.9 entry made the same promise for `orb_greater` specifically -- this file is that promise kept, not a second, competing recipe table. `item_db.gd` reads both files and merges them into one `recipe()`/`recipe_ids()` surface, so nothing else (craft_panel.gd, game_state.gd) has to know there are two files on disk.
_comment_unlock: None of these are `unlocked_by`-gated, unlike `orb_basic` (Tam specifically has to teach that one). The real gate here is Rootstone itself: nothing below can be crafted without it, and Rootstone is quarry-locked content (SD16, a sibling item) reached by playing into Band 2 -- a second flag on top of that would gate the same door twice. This matches `potion_small`'s own precedent: a recipe with nothing to teach ships known from the first minute, per recipes.json's `_comment_unlock`.
_comment_tier: MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md 10/11 and GAME_DESIGN.md 32's non-goals ('large crafting tree') both bound this file: every recipe below improves something the player can already own by this point in a normal playthrough (an orb tier, a tool, a saddle component) rather than opening a new system. Four recipes, not forty.
_comment_costs: Every `cost` and `bonus` value in this file is TUNABLE, same as `data/recipes/recipes.json`'s own base tier -- picked to feel like a real step up from the base tier (roughly double the material investment, plus Rootstone itself) without being balanced against a Rootstone gather rate nothing has measured yet.

orb_greater.name: Greater Orb
orb_greater.blurb: Doubled tether bands, rootstone-braced. Closes R4.9's honest remainder -- the tier ladder finally has a way in.
orb_greater._comment: R4.9 built the mechanic (`data/config/catching.json`'s `orb_greater` entry, a real 1.6x multiplier `catch_math.gd` already reads) and the item (`items.json`), and shipped with no acquisition path on purpose, naming this exact recipe as the thing that would close it. Cost mirrors `orb_basic` (wood+fiber) with Rootstone added and roughly doubled base materials -- a meaningfully bigger ask for a meaningfully better orb, same affordability logic GAME_DESIGN.md 15 asks for at the basic tier.

reinforce_axe.name: Reinforce Axe
reinforce_axe.blurb: Rootstone wedges driven into the haft and the edge re-set. Raises the axe's ceiling for good -- it comes back full, and it wears down slower from here.
reinforce_axe._comment: The SIMPLEST honest read of 'a rootstone upgrade for axe/pickaxe' that does not invent a second tool-gating system: `inventory.gd::repair_tool()` already restores durability to `max_durability_at()` for free, at no station, so a recipe that only did that again would waste Rootstone matching a button the player already has. A genuinely separate `axe_reinforced` item, by contrast, would need `harvest_logic.gd` to recognise a SECOND tool id for the same `gathered_with: axe` resource -- new gating code, exactly what SD18's brief says to avoid if the plain version needs it. This recipe instead PERMANENTLY raises the max (`durability_bonus`, `inventory.gd::reinforce_tool()`) on the axe already in the satchel and tops it up to the new max in the same action -- a real upgrade to a real owned item, using only the durability plumbing R2.2 already built. `game_state.craft()` special-cases the `reinforce` key: no `output` item is granted, `can_craft`/`craft` require the named tool to actually be owned. Bonus (TUNABLE) is half the axe's own base 40 durability -- a real step, not a rounding error, without doubling it outright.

reinforce_pickaxe.name: Reinforce Pickaxe
reinforce_pickaxe.blurb: Same rootstone treatment as the axe, for the pick. Deeper seams want a tool that lasts.
reinforce_pickaxe._comment: Twin of `reinforce_axe` -- see its own comment for the full reasoning. Same cost and bonus; the pick has no reason to be cheaper or tougher than the axe at this tier.

saddle_frame.name: Saddle Frame
saddle_frame.blurb: The skeleton a real saddle gets built on. Braced with rootstone so it can actually take a rider's weight.
saddle_frame._comment: R6.2's Riding Saddle spec names Rootstone/Ironwood components (backlog: 'the saddle in Rootstone/Ironwood components'). This is SD18's half of that -- an intermediate ITEM and its recipe, consumed by whatever R6.2 eventually builds. No mount/dismount, no riding stat, no saddle item itself -- that is R6.1/R6.2's own scope, not this one's.

saddle.name: Riding Saddle
saddle.blurb: The frame, wrapped and strapped. From here you stop walking everywhere you have already been.
saddle._comment: R6.2, the other half of the promise `saddle_frame` above was built for. Consumes that frame rather than re-buying its Rootstone, which is the entire point of an intermediate component -- the two recipes together cost 8 Rootstone, 8 wood and 10 fiber, the biggest single investment in this file, for the biggest single change to how the Meadows is traversed. Fiber is the heaviest line by count on purpose: the girth, the padding and the straps are what turn a frame into a saddle, and it is the one baseline material a player has no other Band-3 sink for. Everything here is TUNABLE.
saddle._comment_ironwood: IRONWOOD SEAM, for SF31. Spec 3 Band 4 prices riding equipment in Rootstone AND Ironwood; Ironwood does not exist yet (no item, no node, no gather path), and a recipe that costs an item `item_db` cannot resolve is a recipe the craft screen cannot draw -- tests/test_recipes.gd::test_recipe_cost_only_names_real_items() fails on it, correctly. So this ships at the Rootstone price. When SF31 lands, add ONE line to `cost` -- { "id": "ironwood", "n": 2 } -- and take the `wood` count down to 2 to keep the total investment roughly where it is; nothing in scripts/world/riding_controller.gd or anywhere else reads this cost, so that edit is the whole change.
saddle._comment_unlock: TOURNAMENT-1, and the ONE exception to this file's own `_comment_unlock` one level up. It used to read 'No `unlocked_by`... a flag on top would gate the same door a third time', and that argument still holds for every other recipe here -- but the 2026-08-22 owner directive (precedence level 1 in CLAUDE.md's canon list) makes the saddle pattern the village tournament's PRIZE: 'Winning grants the saddle recipe, and an NPC line tells the player the mount species can be ridden.' A prize the player already has is not a prize, so this recipe alone carries a flag. `recipe_saddle` is written by `tournament_final_oskar`'s `reward.flags` (data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json) the moment the final is won, and read back through `item_db.recipe_unlock_flag()`/`game_state.recipe_known()` like `orb_basic`'s.
saddle._comment_unlock_sequencing: So this one recipe is gated twice -- on the flag in the village, and on Rootstone a region later -- and the owner accepted that explicitly. The directive's own words: the reward is 'a promise, not a purchase'. The player wins the pattern before the material for it exists on their map, and that is the intended reason to want rootstone at all. What already taught the player riding exists is unchanged and is now the other half of the same lesson: standing next to a rideable creature without a saddle still draws '<name> needs a Riding Saddle.' through the ordinary interact prompt (scripts/world/riding_controller.gd::interaction_offer).
